extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and literary community interested in submitting or learning about the National Book Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Information and high-level criteria for works considered by the National Book Awards, including categories honored and eligibility timing; intended for authors/publishers considering submission or researching the awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards currently honor the best Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Translated Literature, and Young People’s Literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although other categories have been recognized in the past, the current program recognizes these five categories. For category-specific details and any past category history, see the Foundation's archive and guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing / annual eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles honored are those published each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'Deadlines & Guidelines' for specifics on eligibility, the submissions process, current prizes, and FAQ; publication within the eligible year is implied by the phrasing 'published each year.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission / evaluative aim — celebrate the best writing in America
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Book Awards were established to celebrate the best writing in America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Awards are overseen by the National Book Foundation, a nonprofit whose mission is to celebrate the best of American literature, expand its audience, and enhance the cultural value of great writing in America. This mission frames what the Awards seek to recognize, though specific judging criteria are available via the Foundation's guidelines.
